stem: A level is set up between a benchmark at elevation 100.00 m and a new point. The backsight reading on the benchmark is 1.52 m and the foresight reading on the new point is 2.31 m. What is the elevation of the new point?
eli5: Differential leveling: the height of instrument is the benchmark elevation plus the backsight. The elevation of the new point is the height of instrument minus the foresight. A larger foresight means lower ground.
solution:
Height of instrument = 100.00 + 1.52 = 101.52 m.

Elevation = 101.52 - 2.31 = 99.21 m.

stem: Two road cross-sections 20 m apart have cut areas of 24 m^{2} and 36 m^{2}. Using the average end area method, what is the volume of cut between them?
eli5: The average end area method treats the earthwork between two cross-sections as a prism whose cross-section is the mean of the two end areas: V = L (A_{1} + A_{2}) / 2. It slightly overestimates when the areas differ a lot.

stem: Place each azimuth, measured clockwise from north, on its bearing.
eli5: An azimuth is one angle all the way around the compass from north. A bearing says which half you are in, north or south, then how far you turn toward east or west.
solution:
45° is in the northeast quarter: N 45° E.

135° is 45° short of south, on the east side: S 45° E.

225° is 45° past south, on the west side: S 45° W.

315° is 45° short of north, on the west side: N 45° W.

stem: Place each azimuth, measured clockwise from north, on its bearing.
eli5: An azimuth runs clockwise from north through 360°. A bearing is the acute angle from the north or south line toward east or west. Quadrant by quadrant: 0° to 90° is N (azimuth) E; 90° to 180° is S (180° - azimuth) E; 180° to 270° is S (azimuth - 180°) W; 270° to 360° is N (360° - azimuth) W.
solution:
30° is in the north-east quadrant: N 30° E.

160° is in the south-east quadrant: 180° - 160° = 20°, so S 20° E.

200° is in the south-west quadrant: 200° - 180° = 20°, so S 20° W.

290° is in the north-west quadrant: 360° - 290° = 70°, so N 70° W.

stem: A traverse line is 200.00 m long with an azimuth of 60°. What is its departure (east-west component)?
eli5: Azimuth is measured clockwise from north. Latitude (the north-south component) is L cos(azimuth) and departure (the east-west component) is L sin(azimuth). East and north are positive.
solution:
Departure = L sin(azimuth) = 200.00 × sin 60° = 173.2 m (east).

Latitude = 200.00 × cos 60° = 100.0 m (north).

stem: Offsets from a straight baseline to a curved boundary, measured every 10 m, are 3.2, 4.5, 5.1, 4.0 and 2.6 m. Using the trapezoidal rule, what is the area between the baseline and the boundary?
eli5: The trapezoidal rule treats each strip between adjacent offsets as a trapezoid. Summed, the area is the common interval times (half the first and last offsets plus all the offsets in between). Simpson's 1/3 rule fits parabolas instead and needs an even number of intervals.

stem: Point A has coordinates N 1,000.00, E 2,000.00 and point B has coordinates N 1,400.00, E 2,300.00, in metres. What is the azimuth of the line from A to B?
eli5: The direction between two coordinated points comes from the differences in easting and northing: tan(azimuth) = change in easting / change in northing. The signs of the two differences fix the quadrant, so add 180° or 360° to the calculator result when the line does not run north-east.
solution:
Change in northing = 1,400.00 - 1,000.00 = 400.00 m. Change in easting = 2,300.00 - 2,000.00 = 300.00 m. Both are positive, so the line runs north-east.

Azimuth = arctan(\frac{300.00}{400.00}) = 36.87°.

Length = \sqrt{400.00^{2} + 300.00^{2}} = 500.00 m.
